verses.text: Jesus told them, “I’m telling you the truth: some of you standing here won’t die before you see God’s Kingdom arrive with power.”
Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him up a high mountain, where they were by themselves. There, right in front of them, his appearance changed.
His clothes became dazzling white—brighter than any laundry worker on earth could ever get them. ✨
Elijah and Moses appeared and were talking with Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it’s good that we’re here. Let’s put up three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
He didn’t know what to say; they were all terrified.
A cloud came and covered them, and a voice spoke from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
Suddenly they looked around and saw nobody with them anymore except Jesus.
As they came down the mountain, Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what they’d seen until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
They kept that instruction to themselves, wondering what “rising from the dead” meant.
They asked Jesus, “Why do the legal teachers say Elijah has to come first?”
He said, “Elijah does come first and sets everything right. But then why does Scripture say the Son of Man must suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
“I’m telling you, Elijah has already come, and they did whatever they wanted to him, just as Scripture says.”
When they came back to the disciples, Jesus saw a big crowd around them, and legal teachers arguing with them.
As soon as the crowd saw Jesus, they were amazed and ran over to greet him.
He asked the legal teachers, “What are you arguing with them about?”
Someone in the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought you my son. He has a spirit that keeps him from speaking.
“Whenever it grabs him, it throws him down. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and goes stiff. I asked your disciples to drive it out, but they couldn’t.”
Jesus answered, “Unbelieving generation! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with this? Bring the boy to me.”
They brought him over. When the spirit saw Jesus, it immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground, rolling around and foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been happening?” He said, “Since he was little.
“The spirit often throws him into fire or water to destroy him. If you can do anything, please have compassion on us and help us!”
Jesus told him, “If you can believe? Everything is possible for the one who believes.”
The boy’s father immediately cried out with tears, “I believe! Help me where my faith is weak!”
When Jesus saw the crowd rushing over, he rebuked the unclean spirit: “You spirit that keeps him from hearing and speaking, I command you: come out of him and never go into him again!”
The spirit screamed and threw the boy into a terrible convulsion, then came out. The boy looked like he was dead, and many people said, “He’s dead.”
But Jesus took his hand, helped him up, and the boy stood.
When Jesus went into a house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
He told them, “This kind can come out only through prayer and fasting.”
They left there and traveled through Galilee. Jesus didn’t want anyone to know where they were,
because he was teaching his disciples. He told them, “The Son of Man is being handed over to people. They’ll kill him, and after he’s killed, he’ll rise again on the third day.”
But they didn’t understand what he meant, and they were afraid to ask him.
They came to Capernaum. Once they were inside the house, Jesus asked them, “What were you arguing about on the road?”
They stayed quiet. On the road they’d been arguing about who was the greatest.
Jesus sat down, called the twelve over, and said, “If anyone wants to be first, they must be last of all and servant to everyone.”
He took a little child and stood the child among them. Then he picked the child up in his arms and said:
“Whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me isn’t welcoming only me, but the one who sent me.”
John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name. We told him to stop because he wasn’t following us.”
But Jesus said, “Don’t stop him. Nobody who does a mighty work in my name can turn around and speak evil of me right away.
“Anyone who isn’t against us is with us.
“I’m telling you the truth: whoever gives you even a cup of water because you belong to Christ will certainly receive their reward.
“But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to fall away—it would be better for them to be thrown into the sea with a huge millstone tied around their neck.
“If your hand causes you to fall, cut it off. It’s better to enter life maimed than to go into Gehenna with both hands, into the fire that never goes out,
“‘where the worm doesn’t die, and the fire isn’t put out.’
“If your foot causes you to fall, cut it off. It’s better to enter life crippled than to be thrown into Gehenna with both feet, into the fire that never goes out—
“‘where the worm doesn’t die, and the fire isn’t put out.’
“If your eye causes you to fall, tear it out. It’s better to enter God’s Kingdom with one eye than to be thrown into Gehenna with both eyes,
“‘where the worm doesn’t die, and the fire isn’t put out.’
“Everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt.
“Salt is good. But if salt loses its saltiness, how will you make it salty again? Keep salt among yourselves, and live at peace with one another.”
